name: Ssemble
tagline: Browser based collaborative video editor for short form creators, with auto subtitles, effects and stock assets.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: An agent can absolutely wire ffmpeg to a web page and give you trimming, concatenation and burned-in Whisper subtitles in a session. What it cannot give you in a session is a timeline that feels good: frame accurate scrubbing, instant preview of a cut you have not rendered yet, undo that never corrupts a project, drag and drop layering that behaves the same at 4K as at 720p. Ssemble's actual product is that editing surface running in a browser, plus a library of effects, templates and stock clips somebody licensed, plus multiplayer on a project. Every one of those is a grind rather than a trick, which is exactly the kind of thing one-shot builds are worst at. Build the cutting-and-captioning pipeline if that is the 80 percent you use, but do not pretend it is an editor.
coreLoopDIY: A local web tool that ingests a video, lets you mark keep/cut ranges against a waveform, transcribes with Whisper, and renders a captioned mp4 via ffmpeg.
requirements: faster-whisper model download, a GPU if you value your afternoon
whatYouLose: A real multi-track timeline with transitions, keyframes and layered text
Instant preview: your version renders, then you look at it, then you fix it, then you render again
The licensed stock footage, music, effects and template library
Collaboration: shared projects, comments, review links for a client
Cloud rendering and sharing, so long exports pin your own machine
moatNotes: Timeline editors are the classic case where the hard part is not the feature list, it is the thousand small behaviors that make dragging a clip feel correct.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because editing is an interactive loop, not a batch job. People pay for the moment where you nudge a cut, hear it immediately, and move on, and for not thinking about codecs, fonts, aspect ratios or where the b-roll came from. A DIY pipeline is fine when you already know exactly what the output should be, which is roughly never during an edit. Add a team reviewing the same cut and the price stops being the argument.
notes: An ffmpeg wrapper cuts clips, it does not give you a timeline you enjoy touching. The moat is execution polish plus an asset library someone cleared the rights on, and neither one falls out of a single prompt.
prompt:
Build a local video cutting and captioning tool. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, not negotiable:
- Python 3.11, FastAPI, uvicorn
- ffmpeg and ffprobe via subprocess, no python video libraries
- faster-whisper for transcription, model name from .env (default "small")
- Frontend: one static index.html with vanilla JS and canvas, no build step, no framework
- SQLite via sqlite3 for project state

In scope:
1. POST /projects with a local file path or an upload. Probe duration, fps, resolution, store in SQLite.
2. Generate a waveform PNG (ffmpeg showwavespic) and a thumbnail strip (one frame every 2s) and serve them.
3. Web page: pick a project, see waveform + thumbnail strip, click-drag to mark ranges, toggle each range keep or cut, keyboard shortcuts for play/pause and set in/out. Ranges persist to SQLite immediately.
4. Preview: HTML5 video element with JS that skips over cut ranges during playback, so preview needs no render.
5. POST /transcribe: run faster-whisper on extracted audio, store word-level segments, show them as an editable text list. Editing text updates the stored segments.
6. POST /render: build one ffmpeg command that trims the kept ranges, concatenates them, burns subtitles from a generated .ass file, and writes output mp4 next to the source. Stream progress lines back over Server-Sent Events.
7. Subtitle style config in a single JSON file: font, size, outline, position. Read it at render time.

Out of scope, do not build: multi-track timeline, transitions, effects, stock assets, sharing links, collaboration, mobile UI, auth, GPU cloud rendering.

Rules: secrets and model config in .env, .env.example committed. All state in ./data. Fail loudly with the actual ffmpeg stderr, never swallow it. README with exact install and run commands, plus a note on the model size tradeoff.
